sources.title: First Army trained on new software suite that enhances warfighting capability
Global fires coordination provides multiple strike options for the commander
Army 365 rollout to bolster communications, interoperability
Mirroring home station and deployed mission command systems improves Soldier readiness

applications.name: CPOF — Command Post of the Future
applications.purpose: Collaborative planning and situational awareness. Historical predecessor to CPCE.
applications.access: Legacy mission-command environment; local client and server baseline must be identified.

applications.name: CPCE — Command Post Computing Environment
applications.purpose: Supports a shared operational picture and staff planning.
applications.access: Suite of software and services hosted on associated server infrastructure; confirm the approved user-access method for the fielded version.
applications.owner: Operations / mission-command application and server owners

applications.name: JADOCS — Joint Automated Deep Operations Coordination System
applications.purpose: Shared situational awareness and joint coordination. This reference covers IT support only.
applications.access: The 2014 source describes software on approved unit laptops; this is not a current installation baseline.

applications.name: AFATDS / Fires Command Web
applications.purpose: Fires planning and coordination software. This reference covers IT support only.
applications.access: The 2014 source distinguishes AFATDS hardware from a browser-based Fires Command Web interface. Confirm the fielded variant.

applications.name: Army 365 — Teams
applications.access: Enterprise-hosted service; approved client, browser and device access depend on current policy.

applications.name: Army 365 — email
applications.access: Enterprise service; determine the approved mail client or browser access with the service desk.

applications.name: Army 365 — SharePoint
applications.access: Enterprise-hosted service; confirm approved access and site permissions with the owner.

applications.name: FSS — identification needed
applications.access: The acronym alone does not identify the application.
applications.owner: Confirm the public full product name or vendor with the application owner.

checks.name: Application will not open
checks.first: Determine whether the problem affects one approved endpoint or several. Confirm the approved software baseline with the endpoint owner.
checks.why: A local launch failure is different from a shared service outage. Do not disable endpoint protection or reinstall blindly.

checks.name: Sign-in fails
checks.first: Determine whether one user, one device or multiple users are affected. Ask the identity owner to check account status, certificate validity and device time through approved procedures.
checks.why: Opening the application does not prove authentication is healthy. Never collect passwords, PINs or private keys.

checks.name: Application opens but shared information is missing
checks.first: Use a dummy training item to compare the local view with an authorized second user. Ask the service owner to verify service health, permissions and the expected data source.
checks.why: A working screen does not prove that shared data is current. Do not assume a routing fault or change firewall rules without evidence.
